timing.note: Apply through the Front Door (866-946-9733). Each review step should take about 30 days once the packet is complete.

steps.title: Contact the OPWDD Front Door
steps.detail: Contact the Front Door at your regional OPWDD office (the NY Office for People With Developmental Disabilities) to say you want services.

steps.title: Get connected to a care coordinator
steps.detail: The Front Door connects you with a Care Coordination Organization (CCO), which helps you through the application.

steps.title: Gather the documents
steps.detail: With the CCO, collect cognitive testing, adaptive assessments and medical records, plus a medical report and a social evaluation from the last 12 months, and a history showing the disability began before age 22.

steps.title: The CCO submits the application
steps.detail: The CCO uploads the documents to OPWDD's system. Only this complete package counts as an application.

steps.title: OPWDD reviews it
steps.detail: Staff review it first. If they can't confirm eligibility, a committee reviews it again and sends a written decision.

steps.title: If denied, ask for another review
steps.detail: The denial letter offers a meeting with staff and a third review. If you asked for Medicaid-funded services, it also offers a Medicaid Fair Hearing.
steps.time: Third review: 30 days, then 10 days to tell you

timing.note: Placement goes by priority (care needs, natural supports, risk of harm) under ADM 2024-03, not first-come.

steps.title: Look at less restrictive options first
steps.detail: The Care Manager must first explore with you whether the person can stay home or live somewhere not certified by OPWDD, with extra supports.

steps.title: Care Manager sends a complete referral
steps.detail: One complete packet goes to the regional Certified Housing Team: the referral form, the Life Plan, a recent medical exam and a psychological report. Incomplete packets aren't accepted.

steps.title: Get the decision and priority level
steps.detail: A Notice of Decision approves or denies certified housing. If approved, the need is set as Emergency, Substantial or Current.
steps.time: Care Manager tells you within 5 days

steps.title: Keep the referral up to date
steps.detail: Update the packet at least once a year and whenever the person's situation changes, or the referral is deactivated.

steps.title: Provider screening and approval to move
steps.detail: A provider with an opening screens the person. The regional office must approve before an offer, and you meet face to face before the move.
steps.time: Screening within 14 days of the packet

steps.title: Appeal a denial if needed
steps.detail: The Notice of Decision explains how to ask for a conference with the regional office and/or a Fair Hearing.
steps.time: 60 days to request a Fair Hearing

timing.item: OPWDD Housing Subsidy transition stipend window
timing.value: 90 days before to 90 days after move
timing.note: Costs must fall in this window.

timing.value: Closed since June 9, 2024; issuance paused Aug 1, 2025
timing.note: Only VASH and Stability Voucher referrals are processed.

steps.title: Know the general list is closed
steps.detail: NYCHA (New York City Housing Authority) isn't taking new Section 8 applications.

steps.title: Already on the list? No action needed
steps.detail: Since Aug 1, 2025, NYCHA has paused issuing vouchers from the general waitlist. No one was removed.

steps.title: Keep your contact info current
steps.detail: Check and update your application on the Self-Service Portal (selfserve.nycha.info), or call 718-707-7771, Mon–Fri, 8am–5pm.

steps.title: Wait for NYCHA to contact you
steps.detail: NYCHA will contact applicants when it starts issuing vouchers again. You must meet the income limits at that time.

steps.title: Ask about the special programs
steps.detail: NYCHA still processes referrals for VASH (veterans) and Stability Vouchers. These come through referrals, not the general list.

timing.note: Confirmation letter within 30 days; renewing keeps the original filing date.

steps.title: Apply online through ApplyNYCHA
steps.detail: Choose a first and second borough and give your household, income and current living situation. No internet? Book a NYCHA Walk-in Center appointment and use a kiosk.

steps.title: Don't send documents yet
steps.detail: NYCHA checks your information later, at your Eligibility Interview.

steps.title: Watch for NYCHA's letter
steps.detail: You'll get a letter after you apply. Check your status on the Self-Service Portal (selfserve.nycha.info).

steps.title: Renew every 24 months
steps.detail: Until you're called for an interview, click "Update/Renew My Case" on the portal every 24 months to stay on the waitlist. You keep your original filing date.

steps.title: Get help if you need it
steps.detail: Call (718) 707-7771, Mon–Fri, 8am–5pm. Never pay money to apply; report scams to NYCHA's Inspector General at 212-306-3355.

timing.value: Public housing 6 months-2 years; Section 8 2-5 years
timing.note: From SHA's FAQ. SHA's Section 8 list is currently closed.

steps.title: Apply online
steps.detail: The Syracuse Housing Authority (SHA) takes applications through its online portal ("Apply Now"). Household income must be within HUD limits.

steps.title: Expect to wait
steps.detail: Public housing usually takes 6 months to 2 years, depending on bedroom size. Section 8 may take 2–5 years. Some emergencies may get priority.

steps.title: Know the Section 8 list is closed now
steps.detail: SHA's Section 8 page says its waiting list is closed. Section 8: (315) 470-4400.

steps.title: If picked for Section 8, finish the full application
steps.detail: SHA checks income and criminal background for all adults. If approved, you get a voucher and time to find a unit.

timing.value: Section 8 closed; public housing open since Aug 31, 2026
timing.note: Preference goes to people who work (or can't because of age or disability) and also live or work in Albany.

steps.title: Know what's open
steps.detail: Section 8 is closed. Since Aug 31, 2026, AHA takes applications for 1- to 5-bedroom public housing, plus Capital Woods, Ida Yarbrough Phase II and Steamboat 20 (rent not based on income).

steps.title: Fill out the online application completely
steps.detail: List everyone in the household, contact details, Social Security numbers and income, and complete the questionnaire about needed features such as accessibility.

steps.title: Understand the preference
steps.detail: Preference goes to working families, or people who can't work due to age or disability, who also live or work in Albany. Others can apply, but AHA says it's unlikely to reach them.

steps.title: Keep your mailing address current
steps.detail: AHA contacts you only by mail. Update your address in writing or with its online update form, not by phone; your file closes if mail can't be delivered.

steps.title: Watch for Section 8 reopening
steps.detail: AHA will publish a Public Notice before reopening the Section 8 list.

timing.value: 1BR list closes Oct 26, 2026 (noon); studio list opens

steps.title: Check which list is open
steps.detail: The 1-bedroom public housing list closes Oct 26, 2026 at noon, and the studio list opens then. Other bedroom sizes are closed. This isn't Section 8.

steps.title: Apply online
steps.detail: Click "Apply Now" at rochesterhousing.org/apply. For a paper application, call (585) 697-7180 ext. 105.

steps.title: Don't rely on the confirmation number
steps.detail: It's only a reference number. It doesn't mean you're on the waitlist.

steps.title: Watch for the Letter of Acknowledgment
steps.detail: Only applicants added to a list get one.

steps.title: Check your status by phone
steps.detail: Waiting List Status Inquiry Line: (585) 697-7574.

timing.note: Not expected to reopen 'for some time'.
Check section8.hcr.ny.gov for open county lists.

steps.title: Know the lottery list is closed
steps.detail: The state's Project-Based Voucher (PBV) lottery list closed July 24 at 5pm. A PBV is rent help tied to a specific apartment.

steps.title: Check the portal for updates
steps.detail: NYS Homes and Community Renewal (HCR) says to keep checking section8.hcr.ny.gov.

steps.title: Apply to individual building lists
steps.detail: Each building usually has its own waiting list, and you can apply to as many as you like, through the local program administrator listed by county.

steps.title: Apply to open Section 8 lists online
steps.detail: Use the MyHousing Portal, or apply on paper through the local program administrator.

steps.title: Call for help
steps.detail: (833) 791-2748, Mon–Fri, 8:30am–4:30pm; TTY (833) 990-4002. HCR will never ask you to pay it directly for deposits or rent.

timing.note: Supply limited. The HPD FAQ is dated Aug 2022; contacts may have changed.

steps.title: Check who qualifies
steps.detail: The household must include someone 18 to 61 with a disability who is homeless or at risk of it, or living in or at risk of entering an institution such as a nursing home.

steps.title: Contact CIDNY or HPD for the form
steps.detail: CIDNY: 1-844-862-7930 or housinghelp@cidny.org. Or ask HPD for an Interest Form: 917-286-4300 or MainstreamVouchers@hpd.nyc.gov. HPD sends it only while taking applications.

steps.title: Get screened by CIDNY
steps.detail: After HPD gets your form, CIDNY calls to check eligibility if vouchers are available, and helps with the application.
steps.time: Within 15 business days, if vouchers are available

steps.title: Gather documents
steps.detail: Proof of disability (a verification form or Social Security disability letter), a letter about the housing situation, and income and assets for everyone in the household.

steps.title: HPD reviews and holds a briefing
steps.detail: If you qualify, HPD schedules a briefing where you get the voucher and a Landlord Package. If denied, HPD mails a notice.

steps.title: Find an apartment before the voucher expires
steps.detail: The voucher lasts 120 days; ask for an extension within 30 days of expiring if needed. The whole process generally takes about 6–18 months.

steps.title: Go to a Homebase office
steps.detail: CityFHEPS is a city rent-help program. Apply through Homebase, a nonprofit working for the city: find an office at nyc.gov/site/hra/help/homebase.page or call 311.

steps.title: Accept other benefits you're offered
steps.detail: The caseworker may send you to apply for other benefits. If you qualify and they're offered, CityFHEPS requires you to accept them.

steps.title: Get your letters
steps.detail: If you're moving, you get a Household Share Letter (just for you) and a Shopping Letter, which you can show landlords and brokers.

steps.title: Find a place before the letter expires
steps.detail: Look for an apartment, room or SRO (single room occupancy) unit within the rent limit on the letter.

steps.title: Contact your caseworker to finish
steps.detail: They send your application to the Department of Social Services, which decides. If approved, you get a letter with your share of the rent.

timing.value: 2024 round: applications July 15–Aug 29; awards Dec 2024; 24-month grants
timing.note: Grants go to local administrators, up to $25,000 per home. The report doesn't say how families apply.

steps.title: Confirm adult OPWDD eligibility
steps.detail: The applicant must be eligible for OPWDD services as an adult and be 23 or older.

steps.title: Take a tour (encouraged)
steps.detail: Camphill encourages families to take a guided tour before applying.

steps.title: Fill out the Resident Application
steps.detail: It covers basic information, medical and other needs, hobbies, interests and concerns.

steps.title: Attend an interview if invited
steps.detail: Family, guardians or social workers come with the applicant to meet one or two Admission Committee members, usually with a tour.

steps.title: Do a four-week trial visit if invited
steps.detail: The applicant lives in the Village for four weeks. Camphill charges a $7,500 fee at the start, since it can't bill OPWDD before someone is a resident.

steps.title: Receive an invitation to join
steps.detail: If it's a good fit, the applicant is invited to join. As of 2023 there was a substantial waiting list.
